claims.statement: For every eligible finite ordinary tree T and rank p with x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, the fixed-selector clone graph with all-clone deletion edges and exactly-two-neighbor support-insertion edges has a matching saturating every upper clone.
claims.scope: Universal ordinary finite trees; F is the fixed set of original leaves v with Delta_p(T-v)<0; clone multiplicity w_F counts active selected-leaf tags; edges are precisely all clone pairs over a one-deletion set-pair or an independent two-for-one support insertion. This mechanism is sufficient and stronger than S(T,p)<=0.
claims.reason: The semantic reduction and strict distinction from old relations are established, and three bounded T_m cases pass; the universal matching claim has no proof or counterexample in the permitted evidence. CB(8,92) remains undecided.

claims.statement: The tagged active-set occurrences for the fixed original selector are bijective with weighted clones, every literal old Delete/Retag edge projects to a deletion edge, and the changed graph strictly enlarges the old projected graph by clone compatibility and legal two-for-one edges.
claims.scope: Ordinary-tree definitions; the clone bijection is rankwise at p+1 and p; strictness is witnessed by the explicit order-14 p=6 switch and explicit clone-fiber example in EVIDENCE.json.
claims.reason: Direct set-theoretic proof gives the bijection, projection, and aggregate identity; explicit exact examples establish strict enlargement. This auxiliary claim does not assert universal weighted Hall or governed RTree transfer.

limitations: The weighted Hall saturation assertion remains unproved and unrefuted.
The T_m results are bounded orbit-flow computations only; the symmetry lift is justified for those cases but does not extend the computed families.
The 241 p6 flows are reported by the pinned audit but were not independently rerun in this seat.
No minimum-cardinality set of switch edges repairing a deficient cut is established.
The expanded graph on CB(8,92) has no supplied exact flow or cut; its supplied capacity envelope is inconclusive.
S(T,p)<=0 does not imply all-cut Hall, and a Hall failure alone does not refute the aggregate.
No ordinary-to-governed RTree adequacy bridge is provided or claimed.
